Question: Puppy born with eyes open does that mean blindness?
Answer: Maybe the pup could face blindness. You need to act immediately to make sure your pup’s eyes are not exposed to light. Keep the whole litter and mom in a very, very dimly lit area. I do not think you could put a blindfold on the pup because mom would lick it off. Call your vet. At birth, a puppy's central nervous system is still developing, including their optical nerves. Because their optical nerves aren't fully developed, they're too delicate for bright light—which is why their eyes remain shut until the nerves are finished developing. What happens if you open a newborn puppies eyes? Remember, you should never force a puppy's eyes open. Every breed, litter and puppy within that litter will open their eyes at their own pace when they are ready. Forcing their eyes open before they are ready can lead to infection, eye damage and even permanent blindness.

Question: What is a traditional Southern-style cornmeal-based "hush puppy," and where does it get its name from (i.e., what was once commonly used to feed dogs)?
Answer: Hush Puppies are delightful to eat, easy to make and are fun to toss to begging dogs (“Hush, puppy), the most logical reason for the name. If you are going fishing and plan on making a shore dinner, then make the batter up in advance, put it into a container, keep it cold and then cook your hush puppies before you cook your fish: Gives you and the pups an appetizer. INGREDIENTS 1 1/2 cups fine- or medium-grind cornmeal 1/2 cup all-purpose flour 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder 1/2 teaspoon baking soda 1/2 teaspoon granulated sugar (optional) 1/2 small yellow onion 1 large egg 1 cup buttermilk 4 cups peanut or vegetable oil, for deep frying TIPS: Cornmeal: If you are using self-rising cornmeal and flour omit the baking powder and salt for the recipe. This will ensure a lighter batter. Add-ins: Add in minced jalapeños or red pepper flakes for a little more heat. Switch out your favorite seasonings to make different variations. Batter Tip: It is best not to over mix the batter. If the batter looks lumpy that is okay. Dropping batter into oil: For an easier way to drop the balls into the batter I like to use a cookie dough scooper to not only for the round balls but also drop them in without using my fingers. It is a cleaner and easier way. Cooking spray: To make it easier when dropping the batter into the oil, simply spray cooking spray on the cookie dough scooper or your spoon that you are using to help relieve the sticky batter into the oil. Oil: I used a peanut oil for taste but it also does the best at high temperatures when deep frying. Vegetable oil or canola oil work well too. Olive oil is not a deep frying oil to use. To test the oil to make sure it is hot enough, drop in one inch batter and see how quickly it fries. It should be 2 to 3 minutes of frying spinning it around. Once the mixture is mixed together evenly continue to add in more hush puppies batter to the hot oil cooking these quickly. Serve with a side of tarter sauce and enjoy! Keep warm: While making several hush puppies, place the hush puppies in an oven safe pan and let them rest in the oven at the lowest temperature (about 200 degrees Fahrenheit). Do not over bake your hush puppies though. The maximum amount of time in the oven is about 15 to 20 minutes.

Answer: Huh? Why? Do you plan on letting your dog run around — free as the wind, to go and come, anywhere and everywhere? If so, then I definitely think spending a dime on a locator collar is too much — you won’t have your dog long enough to make it worth your expense. Our dogs are always under our control. Period. Whether our dogs are playing in their fenced area on our home lawn, or walking on-lead with us down the street or, off-lead, fetching a ball thrown into the pool — never ever are our dogs left to their own devices. Even in U.S. national parks, dogs are required to be on-lead, if they are allowed at all — bears and mountain lions don’t take kindly to dogs. Doesn’t your dog deserve the same?

Question: Should you pluck a dog’s inside ear hair?
Answer: No. Do not pluck a dog’s ear hair. You do need to keep your dog’s ears clean, odor-free and healthy. This is easy, easy. Yes, I spent years worrying about my dog’s ears — always getting infected and needing vet prescriptions to address all the various problems that come with “flop-over ears” — Cocker, Lab, GSD, Mastiff — especially if the dog enjoys swimming. Then a vet in Missoula, MT, introduced us to Zymox — non-prescription “enzyme” stuff that we put in our dog’s ears whenever we think there might be a need. I have used Zymox for over 15 years, with all my dogs, to keep my dog’s ears clean, odor-free and healthy. DO NOT CLEAN THE EAR: The nasty black stuff is what the enzymes eat. We shake the bottle thoroughly and carefully squeeze usually too much Zymox deep into our dog’s ears, one ear and then the other. With each ear we rub outside the ear and gently behind the ear. (This stuff does not burn or irritate, but it must tickle because our dogs want to shake their heads immediately: Head-shaking outside on the grass is OK, but inside it’s best to have some paper towels at hand.) That’s it! Repeat as needed, following the directions on the bottle. We use the cleaner and the hydrocortisone-free stuff: Zymox to keep dog’s ears clean and carefree (Enzymes that clean dirty ears and eliminate infections — put in the dirty ear/s and let the enzymes gently cleanse the ear/s): PET KING BRANDS Zymox Otic Hydrocortisone Free (1.25oz) or Zymox Ear Cleanser Solution for Dogs and Cats, 4oz : Pet Ear Care Supplies : Pet Supplies (Either one is less than $20)

Question: Why does my beagle puppy keep on biting? She is 2 months old.
Answer: Your puppy is 8 weeks old. You write “keep on biting” which tells me that you have had this pup for some time. Your pup was taken away from mom and litter-mates far too soon for the pup to be taught by them how to behave. You need to step up to the plate and be a “puppy parent” not a “puppy playmate.” Your puppy needs to want to obey you, not because of fear, but because of trust, love and joy. As a gal with a lifetime of experience loving and training my dogs, I looked carefully and found this excellent book on amazon. It is available in print and electronic download. “Puppy Training in 7 Easy Steps: Everything You Need to Know to Raise the Perfect Dog”? This title says it all and the book fulfills its promise. Koehler's method works and Bleeding Hearts will bad mouth his method but if you love your dog…” Descriptive overview: “Strictly following the model set out in the “Koehler Method of Dog Training”, some 50 years later, the Koehler method continues to be taught in both class and private training formats. The method is based in the philosophy that a dog acts on its right to choose its actions. Koehler explained that a dog’s learned behavior is an act of choice based on its own learning experience. If you’ve got a pup who will be a big dog, I would strongly advise both. Wishing you and yours stay safe, healthy and happy, Leslie

Name: Leslie Perry Runnels Isbell
Question: What are Welsh Corgis bred for?
Answer: “The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a cattle herding dog breed that originated in Pembrokeshire, Wales. It is one of two breeds known as a Welsh Corgi. Pembroke Welsh Corgis descended from the Spitz family of dogs.” Wikipedia So, what does this mean? To me, it means that a Corgi is a working dog — a herding dog — that will be active, need to have jobs, be independent (has to be self-guided to herd), and strong-willed. A Corgi may look like a cute stuffed animal, but I know from his breeding that a Corgi would not like to team up with me: I need a laid-back, easy-going, happy lazy dog. Is a Corgi for you?

Name: Leslie Perry Runnels Isbell
Question: What are my chances of getting into a condominium association in Florida when my sweet mini doodle dog is 31 lbs in weight and their limit is 20 lbs?
Answer: Don’t ask us: Ask the condo association. Send in some happy photos of your dog and offer to bring in your dog for a personal interview. Tell them what you do to care for your dog, etc. Put all this in writing, a copy for each board member. Then see what happens. If you and your dog are accepted, then you are “home free.” If not, move on: This condo with its uptight board is not worthy of you and your dog. As a former Floridian and Sarasota condo owner, l know that living in a condo can be a joy-filled experience, especially with a competent, good-hearted condo association.

Question: Our Labrador Retriever who is 45 days old bites everything and bites us. Is it natural?
Answer: Puppies are not stuffed animals. Yours is not a “puppy problem”: This is a “people problem.” What your puppy is doing is perfectly natural: YOUR 45-DAY-OLD PUP IS LESS THAN 7 WEEKS OLD!!!!! Your puppy has been deprived of the learning relationship it would have had with its mom and litter-mates: Moms do not put up with biting. Other pups don’t either, so they tussle and fuss and bite each other, soon realizing that biting hurts. Labrador Retrievers are friendly, loving, “play-with-me” dogs — throw the ball! Throw the ball! Perfect “family dogs” they bring fun and joy. The problem is you. Stop. Think. You know what happens when a child’s parents act like “playmates” and deny a child guidance. You are doing the same thing right now with your pup. You need to be a “puppy parent.” Step up to the plate and hit a home run: Teach your puppy how to behave! Name: Leslie Perry Runnels Isbell
Question: Is a GSD or a beagle good for my first dog?
Answer: No. Both a GSD and a beagle are strong-willed working dogs. You obviously know very little about dogs. If you want ever to be successful and happy with a dog, the first thing you need to do is learn about breeds and what they each designed to do. Then learn about dogs — what they need and how to train them. If this is too much for you, then you’ll be happiest if you forget the dog idea entirely.
